news.title: Small Cap Snapshot: Firefly, Krakatoa, Dalaroo, Beetaloo and more...
news.summary:
Here’s a look at some of the small-cap companies making news this Monday.

FireFly Metals has continued to build momentum at its Green Bay copper-gold project in Canada, extending the high-grade core zone with drilling that has intersected mineralisation outside the current resource and closer to surface.

Standout results included 16.4 metres at 9.2% copper equivalent and 15.5 metres at 12.4% copper equivalent.

The new drilling is expected to feed into an updated mineral resource and the definitive feasibility study, both targeted for the March quarter of 2027.

Lumos Diagnostics is expanding the rollout of its FebriDx rapid diagnostic test across the WellStreet Urgent Care network in the United States.

An additional 97 locations are being added, with the company targeting deployment across all of WellStreet’s more than 200 sites by December 31.

WellStreet, the sixth-largest urgent care network in the US, says FebriDx has already helped clinicians make more appropriate antibiotic prescribing decisions.

The expanded rollout will take the number of US sites using FebriDx to 365.

Beetaloo Energy has secured Retention Licence 11 over its Carpentaria shale gas discovery in the Northern Territory, strengthening its tenure over the project and providing a pathway towards a future Production Licence.

The licence also supports Beetaloo Energy’s plans to supply gas under its 10-year agreement with the Northern Territory Government.

Dalaroo Metals has identified new gold mineralisation around 1.25 kilometres from its maiden high-grade discovery at the Bondoki Gold Ridge project in Côte d’Ivoire.

The result broadens the exploration potential around the emerging discovery, with an expanded 1,750-metre diamond drilling program expected to begin within seven days.

Critical Resources is preparing to begin exploration in Suriname following the appointment of geologist Mauricio Felmer to lead its activities in the country.

First-pass soil sampling at the Gado Manda project is targeted to start in December.

The company plans to undertake a low-cost, systematic program, with the results to help prioritise follow-up exploration from January 2027.

Krakatoa records strong results

Krakatoa Resources has returned further high-grade gold and antimony results from its project in Georgia, including a peak gold result of 16.25 grams per tonne.

The company is working towards a maiden mineral resource, while ore sorting test work in Germany is expected to begin this month.
